clue.text: Classical orator upsets Eric in company

indicators.note: in means the shuffled name sits inside the abbreviation for company
upsets means the letters of the name Eric are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: An old orator disturbs a man called Eric at a social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' reads as a crowd of people here, but it is only the usual two-letter business abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Tullius Cicero was the great public speaker of the Roman Republic, a classical orator by example.

clue.text: Girl outwardly competent and very charming

indicators.note: outwardly means the word for competent lies on the outside, wrapping round the girl's name

parts.note: competent means able
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl who is capable on the outside and utterly delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorable is lovable and delightful, a close synonym for being very charming.

clue.text: Paper with lines on it

parts.note: looks like ruled writing paper, but the lines are an actor's lines printed for a play or film

explanation.surface: A sheet of lined paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' pretends to be ruled lines; it means the words actors speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's text, handed to the cast, is the paper carrying every actor's lines of dialogue.

clue.text: Walk unsteadily at different times

definitions.meaning: to totter or lurch along on one's feet
to arrange shifts or start times so they do not coincide

explanation.surface: Someone walks wobbly, at intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both reeling on one's feet and spacing events so they fall at separate times.

clue.text: One in biology class is very bright

definitions.note: describes a person who is exceptionally brilliant; the answer is a noun for such a person

indicators.note: in means the numeral for one goes inside the biology grouping

parts.note: a genus is a class or grouping in biological taxonomy
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: One pupil in the biology class is a star student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside GENUS. 'class' here is a rank in classification, not a school lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of exceptional intellect is called a genius, someone very bright indeed.

clue.text: Be hot, turning crimson and irritated

indicators.note: turning means the letters of 'Be hot' are spun into a new order

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Getting hot, going red in the face and annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bothered means being annoyed or troubled, a synonym of irritated.

clue.text: Only a small number show support

parts.note: only five, a small number, is V in Roman numerals
to show is to indicate

explanation.surface: Just a handful of people turn up to demonstrate backing.
explanation.walkthrough: V is five as a Roman numeral, 'only a small number'.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate a claim is to justify or back it up, so it means support.

clue.text: A reflective attitude taken by a storyteller

indicators.note: reflective means the word for attitude is mirrored and read backwards

parts.note: an attitude is a pose, a posture struck

explanation.surface: A thoughtful stance adopted by a narrator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' looks like thoughtful; here it means mirrored, so the word is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables, a storyteller by example.

clue.text: Hankerings for last of daily bread

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the word daily is taken

parts.note: bread is slang for money, earnings

explanation.surface: Longing for the end of one's daily loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, so it gives EARNINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hankerings and yearnings are both strong longings or cravings, plural synonyms.

clue.text: When to see the moon near the end of August

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: the end of means just the closing letter of August is used

explanation.surface: Advice on moon-watching in late August.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon is chiefly visible after dark, so the time to see it is the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Incentive to knock time off sprint

indicators.note: knock, paired with off, says a letter is struck from the word for sprint
off completes knock off, meaning remove from the word for sprint

parts.note: a sprint is a spurt, a burst of speed

explanation.surface: A reason to shave seconds off a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a goad or stimulus prompting action, a synonym of incentive.

clue.text: Globe covered in solid ice

indicators.note: covered in means the word for globe is enclosed by the word for solid

parts.note: set means firm, solid
an orb is a globe or sphere

explanation.surface: The Earth sealed in a frozen shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice' looks like part of the picture, but it is the definition: a water ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a water ice, a frozen dessert, so ice is a fair synonym.

clue.text: International trade fair certain to get publicity

parts.note: an expo is a large exhibition or trade fair
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A global trade show guaranteed to attract media attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is attention in the media, the state of being made public, so publicity.

clue.text: Is she French?

parts.note: asks about a woman's nationality, but in French 'is she' is ..., giving a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a woman comes from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Translate 'Is she' into French: EST ELLE, run together as a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The French words for 'is she' join to make a female first name, so she is in a sense French.

clue.text: Giving away recently purchased goods

definitions.meaning: informing on someone to the police, betraying them
the items one has just bought

explanation.surface: Handing over the things you have just bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving away' suggests generosity; it is British slang for betraying someone, as in shopping a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses 'shop' to mean inform on, and the noun names the bags of goods just bought.

clue.text: Care for nothing

definitions.meaning: to cherish or be fond of
zero, as in a tennis score

explanation.surface: Not minding about anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennis scores a nil as 'love', hence nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means deep affection as a verb and a score of zero in tennis.

clue.text: Take the lead but quietly drop back later

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to recede is to drop back or withdraw afterwards

explanation.surface: A runner hits the front but then fades back in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to go before others, which is to lead the way.

clue.text: Court awards fortune to railway

parts.note: fortune means luck, chance

explanation.surface: A judge grants a large sum to a railway company.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancery is a division of England's High Court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancery Division is a branch of the English High Court, a court of law.

clue.text: Wayward boy about to betray one's trust

indicators.note: about means the boy's name goes around the word for betray

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
to rat on someone is to betray them

explanation.surface: An unruly lad on the verge of letting someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of'; it is a container signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is unpredictable and wandering, much like wayward conduct.

clue.text: Rome collapsed in excess, may I add

indicators.note: collapsed means the city name Rome falls apart and is rebuilt in another order

parts.note: over means too much, in excess

explanation.surface: A comment on Rome falling through decadence, offered as an afterthought.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreover introduces an additional point, the same job as saying 'may I add'.

clue.text: To have one return a casual hug is sufficient

indicators.note: return means the word one is turned round and read backwards
casual means the letters of hug are loosely thrown into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Getting a friendly hug back is all that is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns ONE into ENO; 'casual' shuffles HUG into UGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough means as much as is needed, a direct synonym of sufficient.

clue.text: The sad gatherings for bereavements

indicators.note: gatherings means the letters of 'The sad' are collected up and regrouped

explanation.surface: Mournful assemblies held for those who have lost loved ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gatherings' looks like funeral gatherings; it signals rearranging THE SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bereavement is the loss of someone through their passing, so the plural matches deaths.

clue.text: Wrongly posted to headquarters

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of posted are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone was sent by mistake to head office.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a base or central store, and in military use a regimental headquarters.

clue.text: An asinine utterance?

parts.note: seems to mean a foolish remark, but asinine literally means of an ass, so it is a donkey's bray

explanation.surface: A silly thing to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'asinine' usually means stupid; literally it means donkey-like.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise a donkey makes is its bray, written as this imitative word.

clue.text: Club that has lofty aims

parts.note: sounds like an ambitious society, but it is an old golf club with a lofted face for hitting the ball high

explanation.surface: A society with high ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, 'loft' is the angle of a club face; the old wooden club with much loft had this name.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned lofted wooden golf club, roughly a modern three-wood, carried this name.

clue.text: Conserve in jar, perhaps, right to the top

parts.note: a conserve is a jam
goods placed in a jar, for example, are packed

explanation.surface: Preserves filled into a jar up to the brim.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crammed full is filled to capacity, right to the top.

clue.text: Wives nag sometimes about unexpected difficulties

indicators.note: about here means round, the letters sit within the phrase 'Wives nag sometimes'

explanation.surface: Wives occasionally complain about unforeseen problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the answer lying within wiveS NAG Sometimes.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unforeseen obstacle or hitch, so the plural means unexpected difficulties.

clue.text: Two men of a bygone age

parts.note: Victor is a man's name
Ian is a second man's name

explanation.surface: A pair of old-fashioned gentlemen.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the era of Queen Victoria's reign, 1837-1901, a past period.
